app.title: AquaScope Dashboard
app.summary: A person loads water data into one shared workspace. It can come from a live agency source chosen by region, from an uploaded CSV or JSON file, or from a demo dataset. They profile the workspace and score its quality, then apply the recommended cleaning steps, which replace the workspace with the cleaned table. Next they plot it or run hydrological analyses on a chosen discharge column: flow duration, baseflow separation with filter parameters, recession, flow signatures, and a frequency fit to annual maxima with bootstrap confidence bounds. Water-quality parameters can also be screened against guideline thresholds. They leave with a return-level table, summary indices and the cleaned workspace, saved as CSV files.

task.text: Bring a water record in, check and clean it, and compute hydrological statistics and design return levels from it.

data.text: Gauge and monitoring records: dated measurements of discharge, water level or water-quality parameters at one or more stations, with coordinates. Some are wide (one column per variable) and some are long (a parameter and a value).
data.item: one dated measurement at a station: a discharge value or a water-quality parameter reading

stage.text: cleaning and analysing a gauge or monitoring record, from a first look through to design values

mechanism.text: Pages in a sidebar menu all work on one workspace table. Loading or cleaning data replaces that table, and every analysis page reads it. On each page, a dropdown picks the analysis or chart, and sliders and radio buttons set the method's parameters. Results appear as metric tiles, interactive Plotly charts and tables, with CSV download buttons.

field.text: streamflow analysis and flood frequency analysis in hydrology

workflow.name: load a measured record, clean it, and compute summary statistics and design values from it

steps.here: Three tabs: live sources (pick a region and a source, fill in that source's own form, press Collect data), an uploaded CSV or JSON, or a 40-year streamflow or 180-day water-quality demo. Whatever is loaded becomes the shared workspace dataset.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: The EDA report shows counts of records, stations and parameters, completeness, a per-parameter table with outlier counts, and a histogram. The Visualize page switches between time series, box plot, correlation heatmap, hydrograph, station map and other charts.

steps.step: find and fix problems in the data
steps.here: Quality assessment scores completeness and duplicates and recommends steps. These are pre-selected in Preprocess (remove duplicates, fill missing, remove outliers, normalise, resample daily). Apply preprocessing then replaces the workspace with the cleaned table.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: The Hydrology Lab picks a discharge column and an analysis: flow duration curve (Q50, Q95), baseflow separation by Lyne-Hollick, Eckhardt or UKIH with sliders for α, passes, BFI_max or block size, recession constant, or 22 flow signatures.

steps.step: fit a distribution to extremes and estimate return levels
steps.here: Extreme Events picks GEV, Log-Pearson III or Gumbel, a confidence level, a number of bootstrap samples and the return periods. It fits the distribution to annual maxima and shows AIC, the KS p-value, and a return-level curve with bounds and empirical points.

steps.step: flag items that break a rule
steps.here: Quality Alerts compares each water-quality parameter with WHO guideline limits. It counts exceedances and marks each parameter OK, Warning (any exceedance) or Alert (more than 10%).
Download return levels (CSV) with lower and upper bounds. The sidebar workspace card downloads the current (cleaned) workspace as CSV.

distinctive: One shared workspace table flows through every page, and cleaning overwrites it, so every later analysis uses the cleaned data
Return levels come with bootstrap confidence bounds, plotted beside empirical annual maxima at Weibull plotting positions
Baseflow separation has three digital-filter methods, each with its own parameter sliders, and reports a baseflow index
Each live source has its own form that blocks submission until required fields are filled, rather than failing on the request
Water-quality samples are screened against fixed WHO guideline limits, with a rule turning exceedance percentages into status classes
